narrative: Demand for PL2__M9CF40FE is smooth and near-normally distributed (CV=0.43, 96.5% non-zero days) with no detectable trend over the observation window. Lead times are short (mean 1.18 days) but moderately variable (CV=0.87), which drives the safety stock requirement. A classical (r,Q) continuous-review policy is adopted, with the EOQ capped at the storage-capacity limit of 43,281 units. The resulting policy cuts annual inventory costs by 83.4% versus the current SAP baseline while achieving the 95% service level target.
warnings: EOQ (54,484) exceeds max_storage_units (43,281.756); order quantity capped to 35,789 units to satisfy capacity constraint.
Safety lead time recommended (1.86 days) is lower than current SAP setting (3.5 days); SAP parameter should be updated.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is smooth (CV=0.43) and nearly continuous (96.5% non-zero), making a fixed-order-quantity (r,Q) model the natural choice. The EOQ framework minimises total ordering and holding costs, and the reorder point incorporates a z-based safety stock to handle combined demand and lead-time uncertainty at the 95% service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity binds the order quantity at 35,789 units (vs. unconstrained EOQ of 54,484). This increases ordering frequency from ~18 to ~28 orders/year, raising annual ordering cost from ~$920 to ~$1,407. The service level is unaffected since safety stock fits within capacity. If demand grows, the capacity constraint will tighten further and may require a storage expansion review.
